scope: Historical snapshot, not a live balance-data mirror. 32 standard-map games, 5 seeds, 192 seats at turn 80. Same top and bottom 8 within each leader as the Order report. Later ownership does not establish an early cause.

abilities.name: The Unbroken Charge
abilities.text: Your units gain +3 combat strength when they attack. Capturing a city heals all your units.

abilities.name: The Royal Army
abilities.text: Gaining a military unit grants science equal to half its strength.

abilities.name: The Hospitals of the King
abilities.text: Freshwater farms gain +1 food and +1 faith for each public work in their city.

abilities.name: The Great City
abilities.text: Gain +1 culture and +1 faith for every four citizens in your empire.

abilities.name: The Medici Bank
abilities.text: Gain +1 renown per turn for every eight gold your empire earns per turn after costs.

abilities.name: Florins
abilities.text: A city builds wonders 10% faster for every gold building in it.

abilities.name: The Gold of Wangara
abilities.text: +2 gold on mines and camps, and +1 gold on every desert hex worked.

abilities.name: The Hajj
abilities.text: Trade routes that begin or end at a city holding a holy site pay +2 gold and +2 faith.
abilities.note: A road with a holy site standing at both ends is paid at both ends.

abilities.name: The Enderun
abilities.text: Each Barracks gives +1 science, and +1 more for every great scholar and great general you have gained this game.

abilities.name: The Great Bombard
abilities.text: Your units gain +5 combat strength against cities. Capturing a city grants science equal to thirty times its population.

abilities.name: The Correct Sounds
abilities.text: Every city gains +1 science and +1 culture for every four citizens.

abilities.name: The Royal Lectures
abilities.text: Each technology you complete grants three turns of renown, with the same share for each family.

boundToTheSoil.name: Bound to the Soil
boundToTheSoil.text: Workers gain +1 charge. Farms gain +1 food and +1 production.

centurions.name: Centurions
centurions.text: Each Elite unit gives +3 strength to your units beside it, and costs 1 less upkeep.

combinedArms.name: Combined Arms
combinedArms.text: Your units gain +3 strength, doubled beside one of your siege units. Siege units beside one of your melee units cannot be attacked in melee.

humanSacrifice.name: Human Sacrifice
humanSacrifice.text: Your towns may levy every two turns instead of every five. Your capital may levy a citizen to perform a rite across your empire.

magisterialTheSteleofDeeds.name: The Stele of Deeds
magisterialTheSteleofDeeds.text: You have one more Wildcard chair for every three wonders you hold, at most two more.

scutage.name: Scutage
scutage.text: Orders you hold but have not seated pay half their yields. You have one fewer Wildcard chair.

theAcademyOfGondishapur.name: The Academy of Gondishapur
theAcademyOfGondishapur.text: Towns with an empire building gain +15% science. +20% production toward empire buildings, except the Magnum Opus and its works.

theApoikia.name: The Apoikia
theApoikia.text: Your gold buys 100% more when buying settlers and workers.

theArthashastra.name: The Arthashastra
theArthashastra.text: You have one more Wildcard chair. The card seated in it counts twice.

theBarmakids.name: The Barmakids
theBarmakids.text: Each great person you have gained gives every town +1 food and +1 production.

theBourgs.name: The Bourgs
theBourgs.text: Towns working a great-person work grow 50% faster.

theCarroccio.name: The Carroccio
theCarroccio.text: Your units gain +1 strength for each wonder you hold, at most +8.

theCensors.name: The Censors
theCensors.text: When the world takes a census, each of your towns gains a citizen. If you lead the census, each of your towns also gains +1 happiness for the rest of the game.

theChoregia.name: The Choregia
theChoregia.text: Culture buildings give +3 culture and +2 renown each.

theColleganza.name: The Colleganza
theColleganza.text: Luxuries you lend in a deal still count for you. Your units lose 4 strength. A luxury you have traded away cannot be traded to a second empire.

theCommanderies.name: The Commanderies
theCommanderies.text: Each of your towns costs 1 less authority, minimum one. Your borders grow 30% more slowly.

theConsularRoads.name: The Consular Roads
theConsularRoads.text: Cities connected to your capital by road and holding a garrison gain +5 science and +5 culture, and are pacified at once.

theCouncilOfTen.name: The Council of Ten
theCouncilOfTen.text: You have two more Wildcard chairs.

theCuratorOfWaters.name: The Curator of Waters
theCuratorOfWaters.text: Public works give +2 happiness and are built 50% faster.

theDelianLeague.name: The Delian League
theDelianLeague.text: Your coastal towns gain +3 production and +3 gold.

theFlyingMoney.name: The Flying Money
theFlyingMoney.text: In towns with a gold building, your gold buys 25% more when buying units and buildings. Your other towns cannot buy them with gold.

theForbiddenSilks.name: The Forbidden Silks
theForbiddenSilks.text: Your luxuries give twice their happiness. You cannot lend luxuries in deals.

theGeorgics.name: The Georgics
theGeorgics.text: Your works count as having stood twice as long. Improvements that have stood for twenty turns gain +1 production.

theGiftOfTheRiver.name: The Gift of the River
theGiftOfTheRiver.text: Worked tiles beside a river gain +1 food and +1 production. Towns away from fresh water cost 3 more happiness.

theGrandCanal.name: The Grand Canal
theGrandCanal.text: Each of your domestic routes carries half of its origin's surplus food to its destination.

theHighlandClans.name: The Highland Clans
theHighlandClans.text: Towns on hills cost 1 less authority. Hills beside a town gain +1 food.

theHouseOfWorship.name: The House of Worship
theHouseOfWorship.text: Your devout towns may hold all four faith houses: the Mosque, the Wat, the Gurdwara and the Dar-e Mehr. Each is bought with faith. Buildings that supply faith give +1 science and +1 culture.

theJinshi.name: The Jinshi
theJinshi.text: You have two more Civic chairs.

theJixianAcademy.name: The Jixian Academy
theJixianAcademy.text: Completing a technology grants culture equal to a fifth of its cost.

theKulliye.name: The Mustansiriya
theKulliye.text: Towns with an Academy may build their own copy of each empire building. +50% production toward empire buildings, except the Magnum Opus and its works.

theLaurionLeases.name: The Laurion Leases
theLaurionLeases.text: Your gold buys 300% more when buying a hex with a resource.

theLawsOfLordShang.name: The Laws of Lord Shang
theLawsOfLordShang.text: While a town builds a military unit, its surplus food goes into the unit instead of into growth.

theMagnaura.name: The Magnaura
theMagnaura.text: Each town gains +2 science for each Civic card you have seated.

theMarianReforms.name: The Marian Reforms
theMarianReforms.text: Your military units cost no upkeep, but your towns build them 25% more slowly. Buying them is unaffected.

theMuda.name: The Muda
theMuda.text: Your trade routes to other empires pay +6 science and +6 culture, and cannot be plundered.

thePandidakterion.name: The Pandidakterion
thePandidakterion.text: Hexes with an Academy have double yields, applied after every other change to the hex.

thePeregrini.name: The Peregrini
thePeregrini.text: Great-person works give +1 food and +1 production to every hex beside them. Laying a great-person work makes your next great person cost 20% less.

thePericleanWorks.name: The Periclean Works
thePericleanWorks.text: Each wonder you hold gives +2 production in every town.

thePeripateticSchool.name: The Peripatetic School
thePeripateticSchool.text: Academies gain +2 science and +2 production. Science buildings and wonders give +30% renown.

thePythagoreanBrotherhood.name: The Pythagorean Brotherhood
thePythagoreanBrotherhood.text: +2 science in every city, doubled in cities with a Shrine.

theRemovalToXianyang.name: The Removal to Xianyang
theRemovalToXianyang.text: Your towns grow 30% faster. Settlers cost twice as much.

theRitesOfZhou.name: The Rites of Zhou
theRitesOfZhou.text: Each town holding a rite gains +2 food and +2 happiness.

theSerapeum.name: The Serapeum
theSerapeum.text: Each of your gods gives twice its effects.

theSogdianColonies.name: The Sogdian Colonies
theSogdianColonies.text: Each town holding your trading post, at home or abroad, gives you +3 culture and +3 renown, favouring merchants.

theSoldiersShare.name: The Soldiers' Share
theSoldiersShare.text: Melee units gain +1 movement and +3 strength.

theSteppeConfederacy.name: The Steppe Confederacy
theSteppeConfederacy.text: +50% production toward mounted units. Mounted units gain +3 strength when attacking a wounded unit.

theTemenos.name: The Temenos
theTemenos.text: The hexes beside your towns with a Shrine gain +1 food and +1 faith.

theTheoricFund.name: The Theoric Fund
theTheoricFund.text: +1 culture for every 3 faith your empire makes.

theTurnpikeTrusts.name: The Turnpike Trusts
theTurnpikeTrusts.text: Your gold buys 100% more when hiring caravans. Hexes with a road gain +1 gold.

theUniversalMonarchy.name: The Universal Monarchy
theUniversalMonarchy.text: Towns you capture cost no authority, including those you already hold. Towns you found from now on cost twice as much authority.

theWorkshopsOfSyracuse.name: The Workshops of Syracuse
theWorkshopsOfSyracuse.text: Your military units gain +5 combat strength. They cost 50% more to build and to buy.
